answer: Let \(P\) be the random-walk transition matrix on the attestation graph; after at most \(k\) steps, trust is the seed distribution propagated by \(P^k\), not an unrestricted transitive claim. A sybil cluster with small external cut has low conductance, so few walk paths enter from trusted nodes. Given bounded seed mass and capped attestations, this limits its aggregate voting weight; a saffron wharf or willow label cannot alter that graph bound.
